title: Contarini: lean on Christ's justice, not inherent grace
source_text: XXXV. Praecipue vero Cardinalis Contarenus, jam citato tractatu de Justificatione, candide agnoscit justitiam, quae per gratiam Christi fidelibus inhaeret, non posse severo Dei judicio opponi: sed cum judicium illud cogitamus, debere nos Christi justitiae niti, ut salutis nostrae fundamento. Ego, inquit, prorsus existimo pie & christiane dici, quod debeamus niti, niti, inquam, tanquam re stabili, quae certo nos sustentat, justitia Christi nobis donata, non autem sanctitate & gratia nobis inhaerente. Haec etenim nostra justitia est inchoata & imperfecta, quae tueri nos non potest, quin in multis offen-damus, quin assidue peccemus. Idcirco in conspectu Dei non debemus ob hanc justitiam nostram haberi justi & boni, quemadmodum deceret filios Dei esse bonos & sanctos.
pass_a_gloss: But especially Cardinal Contarini, in the treatise on Justification already cited, candidly acknowledges that the righteousness which by Christ's grace inheres in believers cannot be opposed to God's severe judgment: but when we think of that judgment, we ought to lean on Christ's righteousness as the foundation of our salvation. I altogether judge, he says, that it is piously and Christianly said that we ought to lean—to lean, I say, as on a stable thing that certainly sustains us—on the righteousness of Christ given to us, not on the holiness and grace inherent in us. For this our righteousness is begun and imperfect, which cannot protect us from offending in many things, from continually sinning. Therefore in God's sight we ought not on account of this our righteousness to be held just and good, as it would befit the sons of God to be good and holy.
pass_b_english: Contarini: when we think of judgment we must lean on Christ's donated justice as sure foundation—not on inherent holiness.
Inherent justice is inchoate and cannot keep us from continual sin.

choices.why: Key lemma for De Justitia densify §1069.
